South Korea has confirmed its first cholera case in 10 years, with health authorities investigating a suspected locally acquired infection in the southeastern city of Changwon. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency announced the case on Friday, November 20, saying the patient had no history of overseas travel in the preceding two months. According to the agency, as reported by SBS World News, the patient visited a hospital emergency department in Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province, on November 6 after developing vomiting and diarrhoea. The hospital suspected cholera and reported the case on November 9. “Although the initial test returned negative on November 16, a retest of a sample collected before the patient received antibiotics confirmed the infection on November 18,” it said. The country also experienced a larger outbreak in 2001, which sickened at least 162 people,” SBS reported. Cholera is primarily transmitted through contaminated food or water and, in rare cases, through direct contact with an infected person’s faeces or vomit. Severe cases can cause dehydration and shock, which may be fatal if treatment is delayed. The health agency urged residents to drink safe water, eat thoroughly cooked food, wash their hands properly and wash or peel fruits and vegetables. It also advised medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.
